title: Why Japanese Businesses Are Investing in India
paragraphs: With 1.5 billion people calling it home, India is now the most populous country in the world — and it's seeing fast economic growth.
It also has the world's second-largest number of English speakers, just behind the US, making it easy for many international companies to do business there.
Add to this a growing middle class with money to spend, and you get a country that's attracting a lot of foreign investment — including from Japanese companies.
A number of Japanese retailers are now operating in Indian cities like Mumbai and Delhi. These include internationally recognized brands like Uniqlo, Muji and Onitsuka Tiger.

Lawson also plans to open 10,000 convenience stores in the country by 2050, and the BBC reports that smaller companies are finding a place in India too. Furniture company Nitori has recently entered the Indian market, for example.
Japanese investment in India doesn't end with retail either.

In July of this year, Nikkei Asia reported that the Japan Bank for International Cooperation (JBIC), along with Sumitomo Mitsui Banking Corporation (SMBC) and other financial institutions, would be loaning up to about $500 million to help develop India's power grid.
Last year, Japan's MUFG bank also bought 20% of Indian lending company Shriram Finance for $4.4 billion. This was the biggest-ever foreign investment in India's financial sector.
SMBC also became the largest shareholder in India's Yes Bank after buying 20% of it for $1.6 billion. Added to shares SMBC already had, it now owns 24% of the Indian bank.
Supported by a number of economic agreements that have been put in place between the two nations, Japan is now the fifth largest source of direct foreign investment in India.

In fact, in a 2025 JBIC survey, Japanese manufacturing companies named India as the most promising country for overseas business growth — taking over from China, which had topped the list for the previous three years. So more investment may be on the way!
